headline: Tesla Semi enters volume production nearly a decade after its 2017 unveiling
summary: After years of delays, the Tesla Semi is now in volume production with first deliveries starting this week. Tesla held an event to showcase the truck and announce new customers.
details: The Tesla Semi, first introduced as a concept in 2017, has finally entered volume production as of April 2026. This comes nearly a decade after its initial unveiling, with first customer deliveries beginning this week.

Tesla hosted an event at its new Semi factory next to Gigafactory Nevada, stating a production capacity of 50,000 trucks annually. The event announced new customers including PepsiCo, US Foods, DHL, WattEV, ABF, Einride, IMC, and OK Produce.

Despite the event, several key details remain unconfirmed, such as updated order numbers and current pricing. The long-range version is rumored to cost around $290,000, a significant increase from initial estimates.

Production was originally slated for 2019 but faced delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic and global parts shortages. A handful of trucks were delivered to PepsiCo in 2022, but these were pilot units built on a manual line.

In 2017, Tesla advertised starting prices of $150,000 for the 300-mile version and $180,000 for the 500-mile model. While these prices were never officially updated, reports earlier this year quoted customers $290,000 for the 500-mile range.

Over the last three years, Tesla refined the Semi's design, reducing its weight by nearly 1,000 lbs. The final production design, revealed in February 2026, includes a Standard Range truck with 325 miles and a Long Range version with 500 miles, both at an 82,000-lb gross combination weight.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk, though absent from the event, praised the Semi in a pre-recorded message as a "revolutionary truck" and "the funnest truck to drive." He highlighted its ability to carry heavy loads over long distances with ease of recharge via the Megacharger.

Tesla's Director of Semi Truck Engineering, Dan Priestley, confirmed the 500-mile range is achieved with fully loaded trucks. Lighter loads of around 60,000 pounds could potentially extend the range to 600 miles, with multiple configurations planned for various applications.

headline: Microsoft is killing off the 'Copilot Plus PC' brand
summary: Despite new Surface devices meeting the technical requirements, Microsoft and Qualcomm confirm they are moving away from the 'Copilot Plus PC' branding. The brand's flagship feature, Recall, faced criticism.
details: Microsoft and Qualcomm are reportedly admitting that the 'Copilot Plus PC' brand is already dead, just two and a half years after its introduction. This comes despite new 12-inch Microsoft Surface Pro and 13-inch Surface Laptop models technically meeting the system requirements.

Microsoft Surface CVP Brett Ostrom confirmed that these new devices are not being called Copilot Plus PCs. Qualcomm's SVP of compute and gaming, Kedar Kondap, also indicated that future computers offering similar experiences will 'probably' not use that branding anymore.

The decision to back away from the brand is not surprising, as experts noted that nearly every PC would soon contain the basic AI hardware it was meant to highlight. The brand's flagship feature, Microsoft's Recall, was poorly received, and the company faced criticism for constant AI upsells and the dedicated Copilot keyboard key.

Microsoft's flagship hardware is now expected to feature Nvidia chips, potentially ushering in a new era of personal AI in Windows. A new brand is anticipated on October 7th, when Microsoft hosts a 'conversation on how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC'.
